newsitem.title: USA: U.S. West Coast prods mostly lower on thin buying.
newsitem.headline: U.S. West Coast prods mostly lower on thin buying.

text.p: U.S. West Coast product prices were mostly lower Monday, brokers said, nudged down by weak buying after NYMEX crude fell to a nine-month low.
West Coast traders avoided inking spot deals due to the "up and down fluctuations of the Merc," one broker said.
NYMEX crude continued its 20 percent slide in the last month, hitting $19.96, a low not seen since late June, traders said.
In products, gasoline dropped as low as 1.31 cents a gallon, before trimming loses to finish 0.79 cents lower at 61.77 cents.
Conventional unleaded gasoline in Los Angeles was talked one cent lower Monday at 68 to 69 cents a gallon, with no deals heard done.
Traders heard deals done for Los Angeles CARB unleaded gasoline at 73, 72.50 and 72.25 cents a gallon Monday.
The range for L.A. CARB widened during the day, with bids as low as 72 cents and offers reaching 74 cents.
But the final range narrowed to 73/74 cents, the same as Friday levels, trader said.
Farther North, Bay area gasoline recovered from an early two-cent fall by ranging 70/71 cents, or one cent off Friday's discussion, traders said.
Lack of buying interest pushed jet fuel down about 3.50 cents a gallon to 61.50/62.50 cents a gallon, brokers said.
One broker said Arco's announced takeover of Thrifty Oil Co's remaining independent gasoline stations on Monday helped push buyers to the sidelines.
Buyers reportedly withdrew followig reports dealer tank wagon prices rose six to seven cents in Los Angeles.
